bullets:
Flock is tightening its rules in response to a growing surveillance backlash
The company is imposing new guardrails on its police tech after reports that officers are abusing it and cities are dropping contracts.
But the changes leave glaring loopholes.

The police-tech giant Flock is announcing today that it will change officers’ access to its nationwide network of license plate readers, in an apparent effort to quell a growing backlash and win back contracts lost...
Several changes aim directly at a problem that has made recent headlines: officers abusing Flock’s technology to stalk and harass current or former romantic partners.
Flock’s 120,000 cameras form a nationwide network that police departments can use, giving officers access to an enormous pool of searchable location data.

posts.title: The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate
posts.summary:
Is it better to cram more compute into each rack or rethink the architecture?
The post The 1-Megawatt Rack Debate appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Hyperscalers including Google, Meta, and Microsoft are collaborating via the OCP 'Mount Diablo' project to standardize 1-megawatt rack architectures.
The transition to 1-megawatt racks necessitates a fundamental shift where the rack is treated as an integrated compute system rather than a passive enclosure.
Key technical hurdles for these high-density racks include managing extreme power delivery, advanced liquid cooling, and the physical limitations of copper-based signaling.
While some argue for distributed, fragmented architectures, the industry is currently prioritizing dense, rack-scale designs to support the escalating power and compute demands of AI workloads.

posts.title: Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip
posts.summary:
As AI clusters push beyond rack-scale limits, optical interconnects and circuit switching are reshaping how data centers scale. 
The post Copper’s Grip On AI Scaling Is Starting To Slip appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Copper interconnects are reaching physical limits regarding signal loss and power consumption, forcing a shift toward optical interconnects even within the rack.
New scaling terminology is emerging, including 'scale-in,' which refers to the bandwidth capacity maintained within a single chassis to prevent GPU underutilization.
Optical circuit switching (OCS) is being adopted by major players like Google to reduce latency and improve the efficiency of AI clusters that currently suffer from high idle times.
The traditional distinction between copper-based 'scale-up' and optical 'scale-out' is blurring as AI clusters expand across multiple racks, necessitating fiber-based solutions for longer distances.

posts.title: What Will It Take To Deploy CPO At Scale?
posts.summary:
The path to widespread deployment of co-packaged optics depends on solving challenges in manufacturing, testing, and operations.
The post What Will It Take To Deploy CPO At Scale? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Co-packaged optics (CPO) are transitioning from prototypes to production, initially targeting scale-out switch ASICs where copper bandwidth is insufficient.
Widespread adoption of CPO requires solving complex ecosystem challenges, including establishing reliable supply chains, standardized manufacturing processes, and scalable testing protocols.
The industry is currently focused on moving CPO from switch-based applications to 'scale-up' networks, which aim to unify thousands of XPUs into a single, low-latency compute engine.

Commercial success for CPO depends on achieving cost-performance parity through wavelength multiplication and higher port density, moving beyond the current reliance on standard networking technologies.

posts.title: BYD's flash charging Qin Max sedan goes on sale in China for under $15,000
posts.summary:
The BYD Qin Max is the flagship of the Qin family, available in EV and DM-i versions.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD has launched the Qin Max sedan with a starting price of 99,900 yuan ($14,720), positioning it as a flagship model to revitalize the declining sales of its core Qin lineup.
The EV variant features second-generation Blade Battery technology, enabling ultra-fast charging that reaches 97% capacity in just nine minutes.
The DM-i plug-in hybrid version achieves a combined range of 2,370 km and a fuel consumption rate of 2.59 liters per 100 km, setting a new efficiency benchmark for its class.
The vehicle integrates advanced driver-assistance systems via the 'God's Eye B' LiDAR platform and includes a proprietary AI agent, Didi Xia, to enhance the user experience for younger demographics.
